chosen.premise: When Gengar hides nearby, it steals surrounding heat and can cool the area by nearly 10 degrees Fahrenheit.
chosen.hook: A hidden Gengar can drop the temperature nearly 10 degrees.
chosen.visualIdea: A thermometer plunges nearly 10°F as an invisible Gengar silhouette appears in the room.
chosen.note: The nearly 10°F detail is concrete and well supported, but temperature-draining is a broader ghost-like mechanic and is less inherently dramatic on screen than the overtaking shadow.

candidates.premise: Gengar can pretend to be your shadow—then suddenly run past and overtake it under a streetlight.
candidates.hook: What if your shadow suddenly sprinted past you?
candidates.visualIdea: A streetlight casts a human shadow before a second shadow races past and overtakes it.
candidates.note: A highly Gengar-specific physical gag: its shadow impersonation can become a second shadow that overtakes the victim. The Ruby and Emerald entries directly support the premise and make the streetlight visual obvious.

candidates.premise: Gengar may have once been human, and now tries to create a traveling companion by taking human lives.
candidates.hook: Gengar may be searching for company because it was once human.
candidates.visualIdea: A lonely Gengar follows a traveler, then the reveal connects its former humanity to its deadly search for company.
candidates.note: The former-human explanation and lethal search for companionship are unusually disturbing and specific to Gengar. Support is strong, though the wording is framed as an apparent in-universe claim rather than an unequivocal fact.

candidates.premise: On a full moon, Gengar can make shadows move on their own—and laugh at the people they frighten.
candidates.hook: If your shadow laughs under a full moon, Gengar is responsible.
candidates.visualIdea: A full moon illuminates still shadows; one begins moving, turns toward the viewer, and starts laughing.
candidates.note: A strong horror image combining full moon, autonomous shadows, and laughter. It is well supported across entries, though it overlaps somewhat with the sharper and more unusual shadow-overtaking premise.

candidates.premise: Gengar’s Gigantamax form grows from 1.5 meters and 40.5 kilograms to 20 meters and 1,000 kilograms.
candidates.hook: Gengar’s giant form is over 13 times taller and nearly 25 times heavier.
candidates.visualIdea: Base Gengar scales beside a human, then expands to 20 meters while a weight counter hits 1,000 kilograms.
candidates.note: The measurements and scale comparison are fully supported and easy to visualize, but giant-form size escalation is a common Pokémon angle and says less about why Gengar is memorable.

candidates.premise: Haunter reaches level 25 from Gastly, but becoming Gengar requires a trade instead of another level.
candidates.hook: Gengar does not evolve by leveling up—it requires a trade.
candidates.visualIdea: Gastly levels into Haunter at 25, then the evolution screen pauses until two players trade.
candidates.note: The evolution contrast is clear and supported, but trade evolution is not uniquely Gengar and mainly appeals to game-mechanic audiences rather than revealing something distinctive about its identity.

rounds.request: N/A—the chosen angle is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need to preserve Gengar-specific evidence while adding an equally concrete, visually startling contradiction or reveal.
